name: Kartitsch
kurzbeschreibung: Austria's first certified winter walking village and Mountaineering Village in East Tyrol's Gailtal, framed by the Carnic Alps.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kartitsch sits proudly at an elevation of 1,356 metres in the Tyrolean Gailtal, the western high-valley sector of the Lesachtal in East Tyrol's Lienz district. As the highest village in the valley, this community of roughly 770 residents nestles against sunny south-facing slopes between the jagged Carnic Main Ridge to the south and the forested crests of the Gailtal Alps to the north. Kartitsch has wholeheartedly embraced gentle, nature-oriented tourism. As an official member of the Alpine Club's prestigious Mountaineering Villages and Austria's very first certified Winter Walking Village, the community has deliberately avoided sprawling hotel complexes and bustling mega ski arenas. Heritage farmsteads, distinctive wooden drying racks known as Harpfen, and sweeping vistas toward the Lienz Dolomites bestow an unmistakable alpine atmosphere.

History

The settlement history of this high valley reaches deep into antiquity. In 965 AD, the locality was recorded for the first time in a deed of gift from Innichen Abbey under the name 'Kartisa', derived from the late Latin word for a quarter section. In 1316, the village appeared in the Innichen register as 'in villa in Kartitsch'. During the First World War between 1915 and 1918, the Carnic Main Ridge formed the frontline between Austro-Hungarian and Italian forces. Numerous trenches, caverns, and wartime climbing trails remain preserved as solemn reminders, now forming the basis of the cross-border Carnic Peace Trail. The spiritual focal point is the late-Gothic Parish Church of Saint Leonard, consecrated in 1479 with an exquisite stellar ribbed vault. Perched high above the hamlet of Hollbruck stands the Baroque pilgrimage church of Maria Hilf, erected around 1680 following a reported miracle.

Getting There

Reaching Kartitsch by car from the north and east is simple via Lienz on the B100 Drautal Highway to Tassenbach, where the B111 Gailtalstraße branches off, ascending gently for six kilometres into Kartitsch. Arriving from South Tyrol in Italy, drivers follow the Puster Valley route through Innichen and Sillian to Tassenbach before turning into the Gailtal. Rail passengers take the Pustertal Railway to Tassenbach or Sillian stations. Directly outside the platforms, VVT regional bus route 965 operates multiple daily connections servicing all hamlets of Kartitsch onward to Obertilliach. A well-coordinated local network of hiking buses and taxis ensures effortless mobility without a car.

Tips

As Austria's premier Winter Walking Village, Kartitsch enchants cold-weather visitors with more than 50 kilometres of daily cleared winter trails, including the scenic Dorfberg Panorama Trail. Nordic skiers can glide along the 60-kilometre Grenzlandloipe track network linking the Gailtal and Lesachtal with reliable snow. In the summer months, the remarkable Obstanser Ice Cave at over 2,100 metres altitude stands out as East Tyrol's only accessible ice cave, open for guided exploration with headlamps. Just above lies the pristine Obstanser See lake and the welcoming Obstansersee Hut at 2,304 metres, a classic stop along the celebrated Carnic High Trail. A peaceful cultural excursion leads to the pilgrimage church of Maria Hilf in Hollbruck, commanding wonderful panoramas across the Lienz Dolomites.
